display.purpose: Semantic headings on secondary working surfaces; no giant headline on the overview.

brand.purpose: Quiet text-only aphelion OS label aligned at the left header inset; no orbital mark.

prompt.purpose: Italic Cormorant Garamond prompt in the broad shallow composer.

content.purpose: Readable overview response content with generous line spacing.

label.purpose: Small serif connection labels on the immersive overview.

utility.purpose: Compact sans-serif actions within secondary tools.

shadows.name: floating-glass
shadows.purpose: Soft peripheral depth and faint light-catching inset edge.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal tool priority above the persistent world.

shadows.name: active-navigation-dot
shadows.purpose: Tiny light-catching point under the active navigation label.

motion.name: heading-spring
motion.purpose: Shared semantic-heading entrance; reduced motion renders plain headings.

motion.name: immersive-motion
motion.value: speed: 1.4; source Neuron spin and wobble; autorotate: false
motion.purpose: Source procedural Neuron motion; freeze time, morph, rotation, and pointer translation for pause or reduced motion.

motion.name: immersive-pointer-translation
motion.value: x: pointer.x * .055; y: pointer.y * .035; response: min(1, dt * 3)
motion.purpose: Small pointer-driven translation of the sculpture, disabled by reduced motion.

motion.name: cursor-ghost-trail
motion.value: count: 6; size: 26px; head follow: .26; max blur: 5px; fade: min(1, distance / 13)
motion.purpose: Additive arrows disappear at rest; native cursor remains visible.

motion.name: surface-state-changes
motion.purpose: Legacy decorative CSS motion is retired; spring headings and managed graphics/cursor loops own motion.

motion.name: stable-markdown-headings
motion.purpose: Streaming and telemetry preserve completed one-time heading entrances.

narrative.overview:
Aphelion is a black observatory inhabited by the user's supplied Neuron particle form. Curling silver filaments, dendrite branches, and bright tip beads occupy the viewport; pale serif typography and thin neutral glass give the user a quiet place to act within it. The supplied Neuron generator and the explicit black-and-white correction are the authority for the particle form and palette. [The earlier reference image](docs/design/aphelion-reference-v1.png) remains a reference for the floating composition only: environment first, composer second, then peripheral agent and vault controls, then navigation.

The world is spacious at rest and becomes denser only when the user opens a working surface, response, inspector, or dialog. Glass remains visibly permeable to the environment. The sculpture is a vault metaphor; particles do not claim a one-to-one mapping to notes. Connection indicators, selected vaults, projects, and agent states must come from the actual runtime.

Independent saved chat and image windows float above the vault. Knowledge uses a searchable library/editor surface. The brand is text only; the dot grid is removed.
keyCharacteristics: A continuous, full-viewport Neuron field with curling filaments, dendrite branches, tip beads, and open black space.
Low-opacity peripheral glass with a slightly frostier command composer.
Pale Cormorant Garamond paired with restrained Manrope utility and reading text.
Slow procedural motion, exact spring heading entrances, and an additive fine-pointer ghost cursor trail.
Quiet working controls with real state and explicit context attachment.

rules.name: The Monochrome Field Rule
rules.body: Keep Neuron, dust, provider marks, connection indicators, glass, and focus treatments neutral. Preserve the supplied generator's branching form.

rules.name: The Honest Signal Rule
rules.body: A status dot or label reports observed runtime state; a decorative particle never implies a real note or connection.

rules.name: The Heading Motion Rule
rules.body: Semantic headings use the shared Heading component and spring-text-engine pinned to (0.1.5), with its @react-spring/web peer. The entrance runs once: opacity (0 → 1), scale (1.4 → 1), blur (6px → 0px), tension (200), friction (24), and word stagger (55ms). Reduced motion renders ordinary visible headings. Body copy stays static. Center the engine's flex container only for centered headings; retain left alignment elsewhere.

rules.name: The Continuous Environment Rule
rules.body: Keep the overview's environment full bleed. Do not wrap it in a visualization card, bordered hero, opaque sidebar, statistics strip, or dashboard card grid.

rules.name: The Thin Material Rule
rules.body: Preserve visible scene continuity through glass. Resolve readability through local tint and brightness control, not opaque panels or decorative glow.

dos: **Do** keep the luminous vault environment dominant, continuous, and visible through peripheral glass.
**Do** preserve the reference's open space, edge-aligned controls, and broad shallow composer.
**Do** use actual runtime state and real vault/project actions for every visible control.
**Do** keep note attachment deliberate and show the selected context before sending.
**Do** use the exact shared heading entrance, native cursor, visible keyboard focus, and reduced-motion fallbacks.
**Do** preserve the supplied Neuron generator, its seed, source camera, and neutral palette.
**Do** load styles in the existing order: legacy scaffold, observatory styling, immersive layout, then monochrome overrides.
donts: **Don't** enclose the overview environment in a card, hero panel, opaque sidebar, card grid, or statistics strip.
**Don't** add a giant marketing headline, heavy neon, thick outlines, or ornamental panel glow.
**Don't** replace the live WebGL environment with the reference image as a flattened background.
**Don't** restore the rejected ribbon atmosphere or use the earlier image to override the supplied Neuron form and black-and-white palette.
**Don't** describe decorative particles as individually mapped notes.
**Don't** fabricate connection labels or treat a ChatGPT website session as the OpenAI API connection.
**Don't** replace the supplied heading spring with CSS keyframes, CSS transitions, or a different animation library.
**Don't** hide or replace the native cursor, intercept input with effects, or run pointer decoration on touch/coarse devices.
